plan.summary: A built-in backrest bench with a lower drawer-base seat, tall slatted backrest, and an attached cantilevered table top on one side.

blocks.name: Drawer-base bench assembly with backrest
blocks.contains: Lower carcass with three drawer fronts, seat-level top, and the full-height vertical slatted backrest panels rising from it.
blocks.reason: The drawer base, its seat top and the backrest read as one built-in bench assembly sharing the same 160 mm wide, 72 mm deep base; the backrest sits on and rises from the base. Single carcass boundary is an assumption based on the continuous outline in the front and side views.

blocks.name: Attached cantilever table top with legs
blocks.contains: Table top at seat-side height extending from the bench side, with its support legs.
blocks.reason: Per the planning rule, the table top serves the bench and is grouped with its supports; it is a separate physical surface cantilevered from the bench side, so it is kept as its own assembly block.

uncertainties: The table top's connection to the bench structure is assumed, not clearly detailed; the leg count of two is an estimate.
The depth of the seat top and whether the backrest is a single carcass with the base is inferred from continuous outlines, not explicit construction.

observations: Two blocks and valid schema. B01 merged the slatted assembly into the bench base.
B02 still separates the attached tabletop with both legs. Owner expects those in the drawer-base block.

plan.summary: An L-shaped kitchen with a main base run, a return wing, upper wall cabinets, a tall storage column and an L-shaped worktop.

blocks.name: Main run lower base carcass with five door fronts
blocks.contains: Lower base cabinet carcass along the main run with five hinged door fronts and the worktop above it.
blocks.reason: Continuous base carcass with five side-by-side door positions; a single carcass with the door fronts shown in the main run elevation. Exceeds the three-position guideline across the width, but the five doors are the clear visible configuration of one continuous run. Boundary between this base run and the drawer column is assumed from the filler strip.

blocks.name: Main run drawer and tall column carcass at the right end
blocks.contains: Tall column with three upper fronts, a middle front, a square front above two base drawers, and the adjacent drawer stack.
blocks.reason: Tall continuous column carcass at the right end of the main run with stacked fronts occupying one front position in width. Its extent is a plausible assumption rather than an explicit boundary.

blocks.name: Left return tall storage cabinet
blocks.contains: Single tall hinged door on a return storage cabinet at the left end of the main run.
blocks.reason: Tall column one front position wide with a single door; separate from the base run by its own construction boundary.

blocks.name: Upper wall cabinet over the main run
blocks.contains: Upper wall cabinet with two wide horizontal lift-up fronts.
blocks.reason: Separately hanging upper unit with two side-by-side fronts; kept separate from the base run.

blocks.name: Second wing hanging cabinet pair
blocks.contains: Two portrait hanging cabinet doors on the second wing.
blocks.reason: Separately hanging unit with two door positions; corner overlap with the main run is unresolved and kept separate.

blocks.name: Second wing base carcass with doors and drawers
blocks.contains: Base carcass of the second wing with four door fronts and a stack of three drawer fronts.
blocks.reason: Continuous base carcass along the second wing with four door positions and one drawer column; the drawer stack occupies a single horizontal position. Exceeds three positions across the width because of the four doors, a deliberate exception for one carcass.

uncertainties: The opening mechanism of the lower square front above the drawers in B02 is unresolved and could be a drawer instead of a hinged front.
Whether the leftmost door of the second wing (F18) is the corner unit shared with the main run is not resolved from the elevations.
The worktop footprint is inferred from the top view and the base runs; its underside support is assumed from the base carcass elevations.
The boundary between the main base run and the right column is inferred from the filler strip rather than an explicit construction line.

observations: Six blocks and one shared worktop, valid schema. Separate hanging unit B05 and lift-up pair B04 match the preferred assemblies.
Two broad base runs remain. B06 still stops at the drawer stack and misses the C20 zone in its locator.
B02 spans three upper positions and the appliance opening, rather than a one-front-width tall column.
The right-hand remainder is not a separate assembly. The worktop locator on V02 sits above the worktop.

plan.summary: A built-in wall-backed vanity/console run with a three-bay drawer base, an open shelf above, a tall mirror panel and a glazed display cabinet at the far end.

blocks.name: Base drawer-bank cabinet with worktop
blocks.contains: Three-bay base carcass with three drawer fronts (F01-F03) and the continuous top/shelf band above them, spanning about 3096 mm.
blocks.reason: The three drawer fronts sit side by side in one continuous base carcass with a shared top, within the three-position allowance. The top surface is the open shelf/worktop extent shown in view-002 and view-007; the shelf band is treated as part of this block because it is the top of the same run. The lower boundary of the carcass includes the plinth; its front type below the drawers is not separately confirmed.

blocks.name: Tall mirror panel
blocks.contains: Vertical mirror panel (plywood backing, laminated face) rising from the base run at the left end.
blocks.reason: Separately hanging/standing vertical panel with no drawer fronts; a fixed surface rather than a cabinet column, so kept as its own assembly.

blocks.name: Glazed display cabinet
blocks.contains: Tall glazed display cabinet at the far right end of the run.
blocks.reason: Separate glazed cabinet construction, not part of the drawer-bank carcass; its fronts are glass rather than drawer/door fronts already counted.

shared_parts.name: Worktop/open shelf top spanning the base run

uncertainties: Tabletop and shelf footprint depth is only partially visible; the plan view was not clearly located, so the full worktop depth is estimated from the elevation.
Lower plinth/base zone below the drawers could not be confirmed as a separate front or open kick; it is kept within B01.
The saved front-count status failed, so the three drawer fronts are taken from the fallible reference and not independently verified against the source.

observations: B01 includes the top and S01 describes a separate top in parallel.
S01 has just one owner and fails validation. B03 follows a cut-off neighboring fragment on the edge of V02.

blocks.name: Left wing display cabinet

blocks.reason: Left wing is a distinct continuous cabinet run; its tall glazed carcass is separate from the central mirror panel per view-004 and view-006 section boundaries.

blocks.name: Central mirror column
blocks.contains: Central mirrored panel column with its base cabinet below.
blocks.reason: Single-width central column of roughly one front position; mirror panel is a fixed surface and not a cabinet front, so no front IDs are assigned.

blocks.name: Right wing display cabinet
blocks.contains: Right glazed display wing with LED-lit shelves, open shelving and base drawer bank.
blocks.reason: Right wing is a separate continuous cabinet run; base drawers below it are part of its carcass.

blocks.name: Base drawer bank

blocks.reason: Lower base spans the corner run from beneath the worktop to the plinth; drawer split across bays is estimated.

blocks.name: End side column
blocks.contains: Narrow tall glazed side column at the right end of the run.
blocks.reason: Narrow tall column one front position wide, separate from the right wing carcass per view-008 plan.
